=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller SPA Positions (SPA-N-001 to SPA-N-016)

**Scope note:** I reviewed all 16 items, not only those marked [OPEN]. The Seller's "[STANDARD]" and "FINAL" labels and its market-context statements are the Seller's characterisation. The Buyer hasn't agreed to them, and the SPA is still under negotiation. Several "[STANDARD]" items are where the Buyer's exposure sits.

**Headline:** Known exposures total about AUD 4.13m (Riverlark 3.2m, bonuses 420k, Ironquay 180k, Sandbar 330k), before on-costs and Bluefen revenue risk. That nearly equals the proposed 4.8m general cap. Known items must be handled through the funds flow, price adjustment, or specific indemnities, not through general warranty claims, which the Seller's disclosure regime would largely defeat.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller position:** Cap at 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims.
- **Buyer wants:** A cap for general warranties at a higher level, with fundamental, tax, and specific indemnity claims outside it. Known matters should sit outside the warranty cap entirely.
- **Recommendation:** **Counter.** Accept 20% only for general warranties, and only if known matters are carved out.
- **Reason:** The cap is within market range for general warranties, but it does nothing for identified exposures.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller position:** De minimis AUD 25,000 per claim; basket AUD 250,000 (about 1.04% of price), with only the excess recoverable.
- **Buyer wants:** A lower basket, preferably a "tipping" basket (once exceeded, recovery from the first dollar), and aggregation of related claims to defeat the de minimis.
- **Recommendation:** **Counter.** Accept the 25k de minimis with aggregation. Reduce the basket to about 0.5% of price (around AUD 120k) and move to a tipping basket.
- **Reason:** A deductible basket of this size removes recovery for a large share of realistic warranty losses.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller position:** 18 months for general claims, with any limitation applying to all Claims.
- **Buyer wants:** 36 months for general warranties, a separate and longer period for fundamental and tax matters, and the longest permitted period for title.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** Counter at 36 months for general warranties.
- **Reason:** 18 months is too short for SaaS warranties, which often surface through audits, billing cycles, or renewals after the first year.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental and title regime
- **Seller position:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer wants:** Title and capacity capped at 100% of price, time limit of at least 6 years (or the longest the parties can contract for), and outside the basket and de minimis.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.**
- **Reason:** Title defects go to whether the Buyer owns what it is paying for, so they cannot be treated like general performance warranties.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller position:** Not addressed. The Seller's limitations, exclusive remedy, and non-reliance terms apply to "all Claims of any nature," which on its face includes fraud.
- **Buyer wants:** An express carve-out so that no cap, basket, time limit, exclusive remedy, or non-reliance clause limits claims for fraud, dishonesty, or wilful concealment.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject as drafted; insert carve-out.**
- **Reason:** Without an express carve-out, the Buyer could be left arguing about whether limitations apply to a claim it has every reason to bring.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter 1.1 and 1.2)
- **Seller position:** General disclosure of the entire data room (to 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers, and public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Specific disclosure only, against specific warranties, with a fair-disclosure standard. No general data-room or public-register disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject** clauses 1.1 and 1.2.
- **Reason:** Disclosing the whole data room would let the Seller argue that almost any problem was "disclosed," which would hollow out the warranties.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier (Clause 8.3)
- **Seller position:** No Buyer claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything discoverable in the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Pro-sandbagging. The Buyer's knowledge should not bar claims, or at minimum the qualifier should apply only to matters specifically disclosed in the Disclosure Letter.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.**
- **Reason:** Combined with the general data-room disclosure, this clause would leave the Buyer with almost no warranty protection, since it is conducting diligence and knows much of what the data room contains.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent (Clause 3 / 6.3; Disclosure Letter 2)
- **Seller position:** Reasonable endeavours to obtain consent; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of counterparty's written consent. No final consent yet. Clause 11.3 conditions not evidenced as satisfied.
- **Buyer wants:** Written Bluefen consent, with clause 11.2 and 11.3 conditions satisfied, as a condition precedent waivable only by the Buyer. If waived, a price holdback or escrow, plus a specific indemnity for loss of the Bluefen contract.
- **Recommendation:** **Counter.** Make consent a CP, and require the conditions in 11.3 to be evidenced.
- **Reason:** Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (about AUD 3.6m), and "reasonable endeavours" does not guarantee the consent.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility (Clause 2 / 7; Disclosure Letter 3)
- **Seller position:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding; discharge and release to be provided "following Completion."
- **Buyer wants:** On a debt-free basis, the facility repaid at Completion from the funds flow, with a payoff letter and release of security (including PPSR discharge) delivered at Completion, and the amount deducted from the price.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject** post-completion release. Require payoff through the funds flow.
- **Reason:** Under a debt-free deal, the Seller should bear this debt, and the Buyer should not take the risk of the bank's security remaining in place after it has paid the price.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses (Disclosure Letter 5)
- **Seller position:** Bonuses of AUD 420,000 are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. Payroll tax and on-costs not addressed.
- **Buyer wants:** The bonuses, plus employer payroll tax, superannuation, and on-costs, treated as debt-like and deducted from the price or paid by the Seller at Completion. A specific indemnity for any related claims.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** Add to the funds flow as a debt-like deduction.
- **Reason:** Completion-triggered bonuses are a cost the Buyer would otherwise bear after paying for a cash-free, debt-free business.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity (Clause 11.1; Disclosure Letter 4)
- **Seller position:** Indemnity limited to the specific SOW 3 payment; described as "adequate." AUD 180,000 open per DD-010, which is not bank verification of non-payment. No payment receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room.
- **Buyer wants:** A broad indemnity for ownership of and claims relating to Ironquay Project Materials, outside the cap and basket. Before signing, payment of the 180k (or a price deduction), a confirmatory IP assignment, and bank evidence of payment status.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject** the limited indemnity. Require clearance or a deduction plus a confirmatory assignment.
- **Reason:** Clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW 3 materials on payment, so the Buyer may not own parts of the platform until the 180k is cleared.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6; Disclosure Letter 6)
- **Seller position:** A "preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material. The disclosure says the export may contain about 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps), that it is not established whether anyone accessed the file, and that notification obligations are unknown.
- **Buyer wants:** Before signing, a forensic report on access and scope, and a privacy assessment of whether the incident is an eligible data breach. Specific indemnity for notification costs, regulatory action, third-party claims, and remediation, outside the cap, basket, and time limits. Warranties that there are no other incidents.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject** the characterisation as immaterial. Require forensic investigation and a specific indemnity.
- **Reason:** Personal information was sent to an unintended external address, and under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) the notifiable data breach process may apply. The Buyer's privacy counsel should confirm the position, including whether the Company is an APP entity and the assessment timing.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (Disclosure Letter 8)
- **Seller position:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 are "ordinary-course operating costs."
- **Buyer wants:** Copies of the contracts, term, termination rights, and change-of-control provisions. Any amounts relating to pre-Completion periods, or non-cancellable commitments outside the ordinary course, treated as debt-like or deducted from the price. Check whether DD-008 and DD-011 double count.
- **Recommendation:** **Counter.** Verify before accepting the ordinary-course characterisation.
- **Reason:** The disclosure itself says it does not establish whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable, or accrued, so the ordinary-course label is unsupported.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller position:** Everything (general, fundamental, title, tax, IP) falls under one regime.
- **Buyer wants:** Separate categories with their own caps, time limits, and basket treatment: general warranties; fundamental and title; tax; IP; specific indemnities (Ironquay, Riverlark, export, bonuses, Bluefen).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** Reinstate separate categories.
- **Reason:** The single-regime approach ignores that the highest-risk items are not general performance warranties.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification (Disclosure Letter 10; DD-012)
- **Seller position:** Title evidenced by the share register at DD-012, which shows Harbourglass as holder of 100% of issued shares.
- **Buyer wants:** The original register and its inspection, a current ASIC company extract, the share transfer and any stamp-duty evidence, a PPSR search over the shares, confirmation of no options or other issued shares, and a title warranty on capacity and authority.
- **Recommendation:** **Counter.** Complete independent verification before signing.
- **Reason:** A register extract is a source document, not proof that Harbourglass holds clean title free of encumbrances.

### SPA-N-016: Tax and IP open terms
- **Seller position:** Tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime." Not agreed by the Buyer.
- **Buyer wants:** A standalone tax warranty package and pre-Completion tax indemnity, surviving until the ATO amendment period has expired (plus a buffer). IP warranties on ownership, non-infringement, and open-source use, under a separate regime with a longer period and a cap above the general cap.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.**
- **Reason:** Tax and IP exposures are often latent and surface long after 18 months, so treating them as general warranties is inappropriate.

---

### Priority actions before the Buyer's mark-up
1. Move the four known liabilities (Riverlark, bonuses with on-costs, Ironquay 180k, Sandbar where applicable) into the funds flow as debt-like deductions or Seller-paid items.
2. Make Bluefen consent and the Riverlark payoff letter conditions precedent.
3. Obtain the export forensic report and set up a specific privacy indemnity.
4. Remove the general data-room disclosure and reverse the buyer-knowledge qualifier.
5. Insert a fraud carve-out and separate fundamental, tax, IP, and specific indemnity categories.

**Caveats:** This is a commercial review of the Seller's draft, not a final legal opinion. The NSW contractual, limitation, and privacy points (especially Privacy Act and APP entity status, payroll tax, and the ATO amendment period) should be confirmed by NSW counsel and the Buyer's tax and privacy advisers before the mark-up is sent.

- **Reason:** Tax and IP exposures are often latent and surface long after 18 months, so treating them as general warranties is inappropriate.

4. Remove the general data-room disclosure and reverse the buyer-knowledge qualifier.
5. Insert a fraud carve-out and separate fundamental, tax, IP, and specific indemnity categories.
